Predict With a Model Suite

Source: R/suite.R
resolve.predict.suite.Rd

Score plots with every loaded target of a suite. The plots are read with the columns the manifest's input contract names; columns renames them for a table that spells them differently. No target column is read: the plots to score carry no answer.

Usage

resolve.predict.suite(
  suite,
  species,
  header = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  batchSize = 4096L,
  keepMembers = FALSE,
  gapFitting = NULL,
  names = NULL,
  maxEditDistance = 1L,
  terrain = NULL
)

Arguments

suite

A Suite from resolve.load_suite().

species

The species records, one row per record: a data.frame or the path of a CSV file.

header

The plots, one row per plot: a data.frame, a CSV path, or NULL. Required when the suite reads plot-level columns (coordinates or covariates); when given it decides which plots are scored and their order. Must be the same kind (data.frame or path) as species.

columns

Named list renaming the manifest's input columns, with keys among plot_id, species_id, abundance, latitude, longitude, genus, family, covariates, categoricals (another key is an error), recorded (a named list of regression target -> the column holding its recorded value, c(latitude, longitude) for a location; adds <target>_recorded to as.data.frame() and recorded to the target, or with gapFitting the gap fit), for gap fitting survey_year, and for terrain correction terrain (a named list of elevation, elevation_1km, slope, slope_1km and uncertainty column names).

batchSize

Forward-pass chunk size per member (default 4096).

keepMembers

Also return every member's own prediction (default FALSE).

gapFitting

NULL (default), TRUE, or a list of gap fitting settings (candidates, k_grid, spatial, matching_seed, n_folds, max_fold_share, matching_sample; see resolve.fit_gaps()): fit each target columns$recorded names from the dataset's own complete plots. Adds <target>_fitted and <target>_fit_method to as.data.frame() and a gap_fit (fitted, method, report) to each fitted target.

names

Resolve the species names against each target's vocabulary before encoding: the path of the release's names.json, which maps entered names and synonyms to the names the models learnt, or TRUE for the vocabularies alone. Each target then carries species_names, a data.frame of the names not found as written and the route each took (see resolve.names()). NULL (default) reads every name as written.

maxEditDistance

With names: the edits a misspelled name may be away from a known name (default 1; 0 turns the spelling step off; 2 can also rename species the models never saw).

terrain

NULL (default), or correct every target the suite gives a terrain correction (altitude, slope) by an elevation model read at the plots: "field" (or TRUE) reads the suite's terrain field at the coordinates, list(source = "grids", grids = dir) elevation grids, "columns" your own values named in columns$terrain. Adds <target>_terrain, the weight of each source and the descriptors read to as.data.frame(), and a terrain result to each corrected target (see resolve.terrain_correction()).

Value

A resolve_suite_predictions list: plot_ids, and targets, a named list with one entry per target holding value (the combined prediction; class codes for a vote, with the class labels in label; a plots x 2 matrix of latitude and longitude in degrees for a spherical mean), agreement, probabilities, dispersion, the recognition columns above, recorded (for a target columns$recorded names: logical, TRUE where the plot records a value, so value is imputed where it is FALSE), members (plots x members, with keepMembers; for a spherical mean a list of latitude and longitude, each plots x members), and the target's units, dispersion_units, status and limit. as.data.frame() flattens it to one row per plot.

Details

Per plot and target the result holds the combined prediction and, each on its own:

  • for a class vote: the share of members naming the winning class (agreement) and the members' mean class probabilities (a tie in votes goes to the tied class with the higher mean probability);

  • for a mean: the members' standard deviation (dispersion), in the target's units;

  • for a circular mean (a bearing): the members' circular standard deviation (dispersion), in the target's units;

  • for a spherical mean (a location): the median great-circle distance of the members from the combined point (dispersion), in km;

  • how much of the plot's species list the target's vocabulary recognises: n_species, n_recognised, recognised_share (by distinct species) and recognised_abundance_share (by abundance).

Agreement and dispersion measure how far the members disagree; they are not calibrated intervals. NA marks a value that is undefined for the plot (a plot with no recorded species has no recognised share).

See also

resolve.load_suite()

Examples

source(system.file("examples", "habitat-suite.R", package = "resolveR"))
resolve.seal_suite(suite_dir)
suite <- resolve.load_suite(suite_dir)
preds <- resolve.predict.suite(suite, species = read.csv(species), header = read.csv(plots))
head(preds$targets$habitat$label)
head(as.data.frame(preds))
